For issuer URLs with path components (e.g., `https://auth.example.com/tenant1`), clients MUST try endpoints in the following priority order:
OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata with path insertion: `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/tenant1`
OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 with path insertion: `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration/tenant1`
OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 path appending: `https://auth.example.com/tenant1/.well-known/openid-configuration`
For issuer URLs without path components (e.g., `https://auth.example.com`), clients MUST try:
OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata: `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`
OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0: `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration`

sentence: Servers SHOULD:
note: 一部: 無効な cursor の扱い。安定した cursor を出すことの Scenario は無い

sentence: Clients SHOULD:
note: 一部: nextCursor が無ければ終わりとして全ページを辿る。ページ分けしない list を許すことは PAGINATION-1 の server 側

sentence: Clients MUST treat cursors as opaque tokens:
Don't make any determination based on cursor value other than whether a non-null value was provided (e.g. an empty string is a valid cursor and thus MUST NOT be treated as the end of results)
Invalid cursors SHOULD result in an error with code -32602 (Invalid params).
